title: Request benchmarks and soft proposals — lean notebook
body:
Context:
Quick working notebook to capture a compact synthesis of customer feedback captured in recent field calls (Jan 2027) and lightweight benchmark requests we should run before wider engineering asks. Focus: requests that impact serving economics (latency/cost) and rollout controls. This is intentionally rough — use for huddle tomorrow and to seed a short experiment/bench list for eng.

Topline themes (voice from customers):
- KV cache surprises: multiple teams reported uneven cache hit rates when prompt prefixes vary (templated prompts + user metadata). Results in token cost spike and latency jitter for multi-turn flows.
- Latency tail sensitivity: 95th–99th percentile tails seen on hosted endpoints after bursty traffic; customers want predictable p95 under 200ms for short completions.
- Quantization trade-offs: Enterprise proof-of-concept teams ask for clearer guidance on quantization profiles that preserve chat coherence for instruction-tuned LLMs.
- Rollout control gaps: customer platform teams requested finer grained canary controls (by route + model-variant) and temporary throttles per-org for burst protection.
- Private deployment checklist friction: several customers struggled with KMS key rotation and audit exporting in private VPC installs.

Representative vignettes (anonymized):
- Fintech customer: long multi-turn assistant; saw KV cache hit rate drop to 22% after adding account-specific metadata to every message -> 2.8x token cost increase month-over-month.
- Marketplace customer: intermittent p99 spikes during peak 11–12 PST window; correlated with sudden uptick in short prompt churn (many tiny requests).

Prioritized asks (soft proposals) — ranked by expected impact and low engineering lift:
1) KV cache diagnostic mode (probe-level): expose a lightweight diagnostic flag that logs prefix similarity and estimated effective cache key cardinality for a short window. Use: helps customers and ops spot cache fracturing without a full rollout. (probe effort: small)
2) Short-completion p95 guardrail: onboard a routing policy that prefers lower-latency model-variants for requests with expected token length < 64. Include a circuit-breaker for p95 breach. (probe effort: small-med)
3) Quantization guidance doc + example profiles: produce two recommended profiles (latency-optimized, fidelity-optimized) with sample evals on chat coherence. Tie to a best-effort cost delta estimate. (probe effort: small)
4) Canary-by-route UI tweak: quick checkbox to scope canary to path patterns and a manual throttle slider. (probe effort: med)
5) Private deployment audit recipe: a 1-page runbook for KMS rotation + export steps and a sample terraform snippet. (probe effort: small)

Benchmark / experiment list (lean):
- KV cache frag test: synthetic job that sends templated (variable metadata) vs stable-prefix prompts; measure hit-rate and token/cost delta over 100k requests. Owner: CS + Applied-ML. Target: repro within 48–72h.
- P95 routing test: run small A/B where short requests are routed to faster-variant and measure p95 and cost delta. Owner: Serving Runtime + Console. Target: 1 week.
- Quantization smoke: run 50-topic chat eval across two quant profiles and baseline float32; measure hallucination rate and coherence score using existing eval harness. Owner: Applied-ML. Target: 2 weeks.

Open questions / risks:
- Diagnostic telemetry privacy: can we make the KV diagnostic sampling sufficiently privacy-safe (no customer PII) and low-overhead? Need input from security.
- Cost offsets: routing to lower-latency variants might increase cost if variants are hotter; need cost modeling before recommending as default.
- Customer expectations: publishing recommended quant profiles will create inbound requests for support; should pair doc with a support playbook.

Suggested next steps (operational):
- Today: circulate this note to eng huddle and ask for quick feasibility thumbs on top 3 probes (Serving runtime, Applied-ML, Console).
- Within 3 days: CS to produce the synthetic prompt sets (anonymized) for KV frag test.
- 7 days: schedule short sync with Security to approve telemetry pattern and with Solutions Eng for private deployment runbook review.

Quick links / references (internal):
- Past thread on kv-cache anomalies: slack: #kv-cache-ops (see pinned Jan 26 messages)
- Existing quantization PRs: github.com/redwood/rv-infer/pulls/489 (for profile templates)
- Canary UX notes: confluence.redwood/sec/canary-ui-ideas (draft)

Notes to self / huddle prompts:
- Who will own the KV frag test infra? (SRE vs applied-ml?)
- Can we get a minimal implementation of the diagnostic flag into a staging-facing runtime in 48h?
- What telemetry limits do security need before we ship diagnostic to customers?

Raw capture snippets from calls (copied):
- "We're fine with slightly less throughput if p95 stabilizes; sudden tail kills user experience."
- "When we added the metadata field the cost jumped — we can't justify that to procurement."
- "We want a single slider to reduce model capacity for a customer for 10 minutes in a bad burst."

For the huddle: propose we pick one probe to run as an immediate experiment (KV cache frag test seems highest signal/low lift). If agreed, I'll coordinate synthetic set and tag JIRA-INF-1287 to track.

---
End of lean notebook. Keep this informal; will iterate into a longer CS <> Eng project brief if we get buy-in.
